answer: This economy earns identity through costly, verifiable work, not free registration. Each agent must solve a cipher challenge bound to the previous epoch's seed, so one entity cannot cheaply branch a single account into thousands. A fresh key needs a voyage of sequential attestations before it carries weight, and three independent staked agents must sponsor it; their collateral is slashed if the newcomer proves a duplicate alias. A public reputation grove stores these edges, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand real proofs plus locked stake. Faking scale becomes dearer than honest work.
